note: Cross-language admission (400) parity fixture for the workspace metadata-write surface (#task:2193): PATCH /api/workspaces/{id} and .../archive. This gate targets the ONE drift-prone boundary between the two implementations -- the exact Zod-3 issue bytes the 400 body carries (`{error:'invalid input', issues:[...]}`). The refusal PRECEDENCE (issue `code`: too_small vs too_big vs custom vs invalid_type) is externally observable here, unlike the name-availability endpoint that collapses every format refusal to `invalid`. The TS oracle (tests/workspace-metadata-write-admission-parity.test.ts) runs UpdateWorkspaceInputSchema/ArchiveWorkspaceInputSchema.safeParse on each `input` body and builds the same envelope FIRST, signing every expected byte against the real Zod authority; the Rust unit test replays each `input` through the private `wire::parse_update_body`/`parse_archive_body` projection and asserts the built 400 body is byte-identical. `input` is the raw request body value verbatim (an object, or a non-object to prove the root type mismatch). Full-route ordering (404/403 before this 400, then 409/200) and the rename message atomicity are Rust-self-guarded in backend-server/tests/workspace_metadata_write_e2e.rs -- they are structural, not byte-drift-prone. The forbidden scalar is written as the JSON escape \u200d (ZERO WIDTH JOINER), never a raw invisible byte.

admitted_note: The ADMITTED half of the same cross-language gate: bodies the schemas ACCEPT, paired with the parsed EDIT they yield. The projection is impl-neutral -- `name` is null or the transformed `{name, key}` display+fold pair, `description` is the tri-state `"untouched"` (key absent) / `"clear"` (explicit null) / `{"set": <string>}` (a string). This pins the drift-prone body->edit STRUCTURE: unknown keys are stripped (a plain `z.object`, not `.strict()`), `description:null` clears while an absent key is untouched, and an admitted name still runs the fold (uppercase folds to its key). The TS oracle signs each `expected` against `.safeParse(input).data` FIRST; the Rust replay projects `parse_update_body`/`parse_archive_body` the same way.

admitted_update.name: a name alone sets the name and leaves the description untouched
a name and a string description set both
a name and an explicit null description rename and clear
a string description alone sets it and leaves the name untouched
an explicit null description alone clears it
an unknown key alongside a name is stripped, not a refusal
a name at exactly the 64 code point cap is admitted
an admitted uppercase name still folds to its lower-case key
an empty-string description is a valid set (not a clear)
a name and an empty-string description set both
an unknown key alongside a description surfaces only the description
a name with a null description and an unknown key renames and clears

admitted_archive.name: the archived flag true is admitted verbatim
the archived flag false is admitted verbatim
an unknown key alongside the archived flag is stripped
